DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.claim: Dhikr can mean honor or renown for a people.
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.anchor: السابع : الذكر بمعنى الشرف قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says that if God followed their whims by commanding polytheism and sins, He would not be God and could not sustain the heavens and earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r1.anchor: معناه ولو كان الله يتبع أهواءهم ويأمر بالشرك والمعاصي لما كان إلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says identifying al-haqq with God, as reported from Ibn Jurayj and Abu Salih, makes the verb 'follow' and the stated corruption difficult to explain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r2.anchor: ومن قال إن الحق في الآية هو الله تعالى وكان قد حكاه عن ابن جريج وأبي صالح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the sounder sense is that truth would conform to their whims; the author invites consideration of this distinction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r3.anchor: وأما نفسه الذي هو الصواب فلو كان طبق أهوائهم لفسد كل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r4.speaker: الجمهور، ابن أبي إسحاق، عيسى بن عمرو، يونس عن أبي عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r4.claim: The readings of the verb in 'We brought them their reminder' vary between first-person plural and singular forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بنون العظمة وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمرو ويونس عن أبي عمرو بياء المتكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r5.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق، عيسى بن عمرو، أبو البر هثيم، أبو حيوة، الجحدري، ابن قطيب، أبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r5.claim: These readers use the second-person form, addressing the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r5.anchor: وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى أيضا وأبو البر هثيم وأبو حيوة والجحدري وابن قطيب وأبو رجاء بتاء الخطاب للرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r6.claim: In one transmission, Abu Amr lengthens the reading atayna-hum, meaning 'We gave them.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r6.anchor: وأبو عمرو في رواية آتيناهم بالمد أي أعطيناهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r7.speaker: الجمهور، ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r7.claim: The majority read bi-dhikrihim as their admonition and clarification; Ibn Abbas is cited for this gloss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r7.anchor: والجمهور بذكرهم أي بوعظهم والبيان لهم قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r8.speaker: عيسى، قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r8.claim: Isa reads dhikrahum with the feminine alif, while Qatada reads nudhakkiruhum as a first-person verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r8.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بذكراهم بألف التأنيث، وقتادة نذكرهم بالنون مضارع ذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r9.claim: Attributing the literal act of coming to God is unsuitable, so the coming is figurative: God's book or messenger came to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p574/r9.anchor: ونسبة الإتيان الحقيقي إلى الله لا تصح، وإنما هو مجاز أي بل آتاهم كتابنا أو رسولنا.

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r1.claim: The majority read the wāw with kasra to break the meeting of two vowelless letters.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r1.anchor: الجمهور على كسر الواو لالتقاء الساكنين

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r2.speaker: ابن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r2.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads the wāw with ḍamma, by analogy with the pronoun wāw, whose kasra was itself analogized to this wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r2.anchor: وابن وثاب بضمها تشبيها بواو الضمير كما كسرت واو الضمير تشبيها بها

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r3.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r3.claim: The common reading uses the first-person plural, with God as speaker; the intended sense is that His messengers brought them the reminder.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r3.anchor: العامة على إسناد الفعل إلى ضمير المتكلم المعظم نفسه

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr has a long vowel in ātaynāhum, meaning we gave them; its second object may be omitted or may be bidhikrihim, with the bāʾ extra.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية " آتيناهم " بالمد بمعنى أعطيناهم

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r5.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r5.claim: These readers also have ataytuhum with first-person singular tāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r5.anchor: وابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر وأبو عمرو أيضا " أتيتهم "

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r6.speaker: أبو البرهسم وأبو حيوة والجحدري وأبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r6.claim: These readers use second-person singular tāʾ, addressing the Messenger.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r6.anchor: وأبو البرهسم وأبو حيوة والجحدري وأبو رجاء " أتيتهم "

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r7.speaker: عيسى
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r7.claim: ʿĪsā reads bidhikrāhum, with the feminine long ā.

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r8.speaker: قتادة
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r8.claim: Qatāda reads nudhakkiruhum, a first-person plural imperfect of the intensive verb; it forms a circumstantial clause in place of the prepositional phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r8.anchor: وقتادة " نذكرهم " بنون المتكلم المعظم نفسه مكان باء الجر

SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r9.claim: Al-Samīn notes that the kharj and kharāj discussion was treated earlier in al-Kahf.
SAMIN-DURR:23:71/r9.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام في " خرجا " و " خراج " في الكهف

ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r1.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r1.claim: The tafsir identifies al-ḥaqq here as God.
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r1.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن الحق هو الله - عز وجل - ويجوز أن يكون الحق

ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r2.claim: Alternatively, al-ḥaqq means the revelation: if revelation followed their wishes, the heavens and earth would be corrupted.
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الحق الأول في قوله: (بل جاءهم بالحق) التنزيل، أي بالتنزيل الذي هو الحق.

ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r3.claim: The reminder is what brings them honor and distinction.
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r3.anchor: وقوله: (بل أتيناهم بذكرهم). أي بما فيه فخرهم وشرفهم،

ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r4.claim: Alternatively, it is the reminder containing a benefit for them if they follow it.
ZAJJAJ:v4p19/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بذكرهم، أي بالذكر الذي فيه حظ لهم لو اتبعوه.

ASAD-NOTES:23:71/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:71/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:71/r1.claim: If truth followed human likes and dislikes, the cosmos and all life would collapse; the divine writ brings their reminder, yet they turn away.
ASAD-NOTES:23:71/r1.anchor: But if the truth [41] were in accord with their own likes a nd dislikes, the heavens

ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n41/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n41/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n41/r1.claim: Here al-haqq means the reality of all creation.

ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n42/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n42/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n42/r1.claim: If the universe, especially human life, were as meaningless and purposeless as deniers imagine, nothing could endure and all would have perished in chaos.
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n42/r1.anchor: if the universe - and, especially, human life had been as devoid of meaning and purpose as they imagine

ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n43/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n43/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n43/r1.claim: Asad renders dhikr as “reminder” here and refers to 21:10 for the term's meaning.
ASAD-NOTES:23:71#n43/r1.anchor: For this rendering of the term dhikr; see note 13 on 21:10.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.claim: The passage rebukes the disbelievers’ carelessness, then reassures the Prophet not to lose hope: he is on the right path, they have strayed, and they will see their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r2.anchor: he should not lose hope because of their stubbornness and arrogance; he is on the right path and these people have deviated from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.claim: The concluding challenge exposes their contradiction: they acknowledge and affirm truth, then state its opposite and go astray.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p269/r6.anchor: on the one hand, they accept and declare the truth, but then they lose their senses and state what is the opposite

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r4.claim: Human desires and truth are radically opposed, with incompatible demands and requirements.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r4.anchor: Both are as far apart from one another as the East and the West. The demands and requisites of both are very different.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r5.claim: If truth were reshaped to their demands, the moral order would collapse because they champion evil, injustice, vice, dishonesty, polytheism, and denial of Judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r5.anchor: advocates of evil instead of good, injustice instead of justice, vice instead of virtue, dishonesty instead of honesty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r6.claim: Admitting polytheism would make the cosmos unsustainable: each deity would take its creation and attack another, as verse 91 explains.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p272/r6.anchor: if such was the case, each deity would have taken his creation and walked away, and would have attacked another

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r1.claim: People want truth to accommodate them, but salvation requires following truth; life requires it regardless of whether it tastes sour or sweet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r1.anchor: If they want life, then they must follow the truth whether it is sour or sweet.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r2.claim: This wording repeats the warning of verse 69: the Qur'an is their divinely given reminder and conclusive communication, not a storyteller's tale.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r2.anchor: sound the same warning that is sounded earlier in verse 69 in different words

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r3.claim: The Qur'an is God's reminder sent to establish the truth conclusively; if they ignore it, earlier nations' fate awaits them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r3.anchor: This is their share of reminder that God has sent them for conclusive communication of the truth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r4.claim: God sent messengers to every nation to remind it of the Hereafter; nations that honored the reminder succeeded, while those that did not were destroyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p273/r4.anchor: Nations which duly valued this reminder succeeded and those which did not were destroyed.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r5.speaker: يحيى
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r5.claim: Yaḥyā reads ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم with ḍamma on wāw; the author calls this rare, since kasra is usual.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة يحيى: "ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم"2، بضم الواو.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r6.claim: The still wāw after fatḥa was assimilated to plural wāw, as in اشتروا الضلالة; conversely, some reciters analogized plural wāw to it and gave it fatḥa.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p97/r6.anchor: الضم في هذه الواو قليل، وإنما بابها الكسر كقراءة الجماعة،

IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r1.claim: Many transmitters reported Abū ʿAmr’s reading, including ʿAlī b. Naṣr, Ḥammād b. Yazīd, ʿAbd al-Wārith, Hārūn b. Mūsā, Saʿīd b. Aws, Yūnus b. Ḥabīb, and others.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r1.anchor: روى عنه القراءة علي بن نصر وحماد بن يزيد وعبد الوارث بن سعيد وهرون بن موسى

IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r2.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r2.claim: Other unnamed people also transmitted a smaller number of readings from Abū ʿAmr; the author omits their names.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p84/r2.anchor: وقد روى غير هؤلاء عنه حروفا ليست على كثرة ما روى هؤلاء فأمسكت عن ذكرهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi explains the hypothetical as God following their desires; that would corrupt the heavens, earth, and all within them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r1.anchor: وقال الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم ﴾ قال يقول لو اتبع الله أهواءهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the Reminder brought to them as the Qur’an.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p47#4/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ﴿ بل أتيناهم بذكرهم ﴾ قال القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r1.claim: The apparent meaning of الحق is the truth brought by the Prophet; following their desires is literal, while the attribution is figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r1.anchor: الحق الذي جاء به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجعل الإتباع حقيقيا والإسناد مجازيا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r2.claim: Another paraphrase makes the Prophet the subject: had he followed their wishes, he would have brought them shirk instead of his revealed message.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r2.anchor: وقيل مآل المعنى لو اتبع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أهواءهم فجاءهم بالشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r3.claim: On the apparent reading, God would have ruined the world and the Resurrection begun in overwhelming anger; the supposition that the Prophet could change revelation is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r3.anchor: أي لخرب الله تعالى العالم وقامت القيامة لفرط غضبه سبحانه وهو فرض محال

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r4.claim: A second analysis takes الحق as what accords with reality about divinity and اتباع metaphorically as agreement: if shirk were true, the heavens and earth would be corrupt, as argued in 21:22.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r4.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالحق الأمر المطابق للواقع في شأن الألوهية والإتباع مجازا عن الموافقة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r5.claim: An objection says this analysis does not suit the context; shirk in divinity does not entail cosmic corruption, which follows from shirk in lordship, unlike Quraysh's belief as indicated in 31:25.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r5.anchor: وهو لا يستلزم الفساد والذي يستلزمه إنما هو الشرك في الربوبية كما تزعمه الثنوية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r6.claim: A broader reading says that if truth in general conformed to their desires, the heavens and earth would lose all order; this digression aptly magnifies truth as the basis of cosmic order.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r6.anchor: لو وافق الحق مطلقا أهواءهم لخرجت السماوات والأرض عن الصلاح والانتظام بالكلية

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r7.claim: A report from Abu Salih, also attributed by some to Ibn Jurayj and by al-Zamakhshari to Qatada, identifies الحق as God: if God legislated shirk to please them, He would not be God and creation would be corrupted.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r7.anchor: وقد أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي صالح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r8.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r8.claim: The God-as-حق interpretation presupposes that legislating shirk is a deficiency from which God must be declared free; al-Khafaji says rational proof establishes this with no disagreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r8.anchor: وقد ذكر ذلك الخفاجي وذكر أنه قد قام الدليل العقلي عليه وأنه لا خلاف فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r9.claim: Al-Alusi defends the God-as-حق reading as contextually apt: their hatred cannot change what God reveals, and it is impossible for the Prophet to be sent with what they prefer over truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r9.anchor: ولعل الكلام عليه اعتراض أيضا للإشارة إلى عدم إمكان إرسال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام إليهم بخلاف ما جاء به

ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r10.claim: A further explanation says indulging their contradictory desires would disorder the world and expose their irrationality; al-Alusi dismisses it with وهو كما ترى.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p52/r10.anchor: لو فعل الله تعالى ما يوافق أهواءهم لاختل نظام العالم لما أن آراءهم متناقضة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r1.speaker: ابن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r1.claim: Ibn Waththab reads the wāw in ولو with ḍamma.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب ( ولو اتبع ) بضم الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r2.claim: The verse shifts from condemning their dislike of truth to condemning their rejection of what every soul naturally wants for its own good.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r2.anchor: انتقال من تشنيعهم بكراهة الحق إلى تشنيعهم بالإعراض عما جبل عليه كل نفس

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r3.claim: The reminder is the Qur'an, their honor and distinction; they should have eagerly accepted their own glory, but turn away from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r3.anchor: والمراد بالذكر القرآن الذي هو فخرهم وشرفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r4.claim: The explicit ذكرهم instead of a pronoun intensifies their rebuke; the فاء makes their turning away follow from God's giving them the reminder.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r4.anchor: وفي وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير مزيد تشنيع لهم وتقريع والفاء لترتيب ما بعدها من إعراضهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r5.claim: If الحق earlier means the Qur'an, God's shift from the Prophet's pronoun to the majestic first-person plural honors the Prophet; calling it truth suits the denial context, while calling it reminder suits divine attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r5.anchor: الإتيان بالذكر إلى نون العظمة بعد إسناده إلى ضميره

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r6.claim: Another interpretation is the scripture they had wished for, saying that with a reminder from earlier peoples they would be God's sincere servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r6.anchor: ما تمنوه بقولهم لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the reminder as admonition; Isa's reading بذكراهم supports this interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بالذكر الوعظ

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r8.claim: Al-Alusi favors the Qur'an-as-honor or wished-for-book readings: turning from either is more blameworthy than turning from admonition.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53/r8.anchor: ورجح القولان الأولان بأن التشنيع عليهما أشد فإن الإعراض عن وعظهم ليس بمثابة إعراضهم عن شرفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi argues that rejecting admonition is also serious because admonition explains how a person's condition can be put right, but calls the contrary objection strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r1.anchor: الوعظ فيه بيان ما يصلح به حال من يوعظ فالتشنيع بالإعراض عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر ووهب حيوة والجحدري وابن قطيب وأبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r2.claim: These readers use the addressed second-person tāʾ, بل أتيتهم, speaking to the Prophet.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر ويونس عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.claim: These readers have بل أتيتهم with first-person singular tāʾ; Ibn Abi Ishaq and Isa also transmit the addressed tāʾ reading, alongside Wuhayb, al-Jahdari, Ibn Qutayb, and Abu Rajaʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر ويونس عن أبي عمرو

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.claim: In one transmission, Abu Amr reads آتيناهم with a long initial alif; this reading needs no ellipsis of a genitive or figurative construal.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r4.anchor: وأبو عمرو في رواية ( آتيناهم ) بالمد ولا حاجة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p53#2/r5.claim: On the majority reading, a genitive may be omitted if the bāʾ means accompaniment; Qatada reads نذكرهم with the first-person plural nūn.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r4.speaker: ابن جريج ومقاتل والسدي وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and others say al-haqq is God: if God followed their wishes in His actions, the heavens and earth would be corrupted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج ومقاتل والسدي وجماعة: "الحق" هو الله، أي: لو اتبع الله مرادهم فيما يفعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r5.claim: Another explanation takes “following their wishes” to mean that God would call a partner or son for Himself as they claim, corrupting the heavens and earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: لو اتبع مرادهم، فسمى لنفسه شريكا وولدا كما يقولون: {لفسدت السماوات والأرض}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r6.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r6.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj identify al-haqq as the Quran: if it descended according to their wishes for partners and offspring, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#2/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء والزجاج: والمراد بالحق القرآن أي: لو نزل القرآن بما يحبون من جعل الشريك والولد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r1.claim: The Quran is what reminds them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r1.anchor: بذكرهم} بما يذكرهم، قال ابن عباس: أي: بما فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says their “reminder” is their honor and distinction, namely the Quran, as in passages calling it their remembrance and honor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي: بما فيه فخرهم وشرفهم، يعني القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r3.claim: Their remembrance here means their honor, from which they turn away.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p424#3/r3.anchor: فهم عن ذكرهم} يعني عن شرفهم، {معرضون}

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r4.claim: If reality accommodated their desire for multiple gods, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r4.anchor: بأن كان في الواقع آلهة شتى

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r5.claim: The argument repeats that multiple gods would corrupt the cosmos.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r5.anchor: لو كان فيهما ءالهة إلا الله لفسدتا

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r6.claim: One reading says that if truth followed their desires and became falsehood, the world's order would vanish and nothing remain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r6.anchor: لو اتبع الحق أهواءهم وانقلب باطلا لذهب ما قام به العالم

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r7.claim: Another says that if Muhammad's truth became their desired idolatry, God would bring the Resurrection and destroy the world in anger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r7.anchor: أو لو اتبع الحق الذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أهواءهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r8.claim: On the Muʿtazilite principle, granting their desire for shirk and sins would make God cease to be God and unable to sustain creation.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r9.claim: Their reminder is the Book, as admonition or renown.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r9.anchor: بالكتاب الذي هو ذكرهم أي وعظهم أو صيتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r10.claim: Alternatively, it is the reminder they had wished for in an earlier claim.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r11.anchor: لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين } وقرىء «بذكراهم»

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r12.claim: They turn away from the reminder instead of attending to it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:70-71/r12.anchor: { فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون } لا يلتفتون إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.claim: The verses eliminate grounds for denial and accusation, leaving hatred of truth or lack of discernment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:72-73/r10.anchor: حصر أقسام ما يؤدي إلى الإنكار والاتهام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r6.claim: If they stopped hating the truth, they would love and follow it, becoming upright and reforming themselves; the hypothetical explains the consequence of their aversion.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r6.anchor: فلو تركوا الكره لأحبوه ولو أحبوه لأتبعوه ولو اتبعوه لانصلحوا وأصلحوا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r7.claim: The author allows the conditional clause to function as a circumstantial clause after “hating,” as Shaykh Saʿd al-Din discusses, or as a conjunction with an implied preceding condition and result.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r7.anchor: ولعله حال من فاعل كاره , فإن جزاءه خبري مسوغ لكونه حالا كما ذكره الشيخ سعد الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r8.claim: Following their whims would ruin creation: multiple gods entail mutual obstruction, and conflicting desires cause disputes and harm until truth restores order by wisdom and subdues them.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r9.claim: Their reminder is the wise Book, which repairs knowledge and order: reflection frees the ignorant from ignorance and guides their conduct, while leading the learned toward perfection and honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r9.anchor: وهو الكتاب الذي في غاية الحكمة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r10.claim: The Book would bring them honor and renown, so their turning away from it only harms them; their rejection brings no loss to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p212/r10.anchor: إنما ضرره عائد إليهم , وراجع في كل حال عليهم

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r3.claim: Abu Salih identifies “the truth” in this clause as God.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r3.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله {أم لم يعرفوا رسولهم} قال: عرفوه ولكن حسدوه وفي قوله {ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم}

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that God has made the reminder clear to them.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {بل أتيناهم بذكرهم} قال: بينا لهم

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r5.claim: Qatada identifies their reminder as the Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {بل أتيناهم بذكرهم} قال: هذا القرآن

DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.claim: Mujahid says the discussion of kharj and the preceding account concerns the Quraysh unbelievers.
DURR-FULL:v6p109/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الخرج وما قبلها من القصة لكفار قريش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r1.claim: The impossible condition follows the statement that most people dislike the truth, intensifying the rebuke: their whims would bring ruin to the world and its inhabitants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r1.anchor: زيادة في التشنيع على أهوائهم فإنها مفضية إلى فساد العالم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r2.claim: Here الحق is the truth just mentioned: what agrees with objective reality and the true nature of things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r2.anchor: والحق هنا هو الحق المتقدم في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r3.claim: هوى is desire for what suits one’s purpose, especially appetites that are not simply part of human nature; ordinary hunger and thirst are not themselves whim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r3.anchor: فسجل عليهم أنهم أهل هوى والهوى شهوة ومحبة لما يلائم غرض صاحبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r4.claim: Whim includes wanting what nature does not require, such as injustice and humiliating people, or pursuing natural appetites in corrupting ways, such as stolen food or illicit sex.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r4.anchor: ليست من الهوى وإنما الهوى شهوة ما لا تقتضيه الفطرة كشهوة الظلم وإهانة الناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r5.claim: Following the truth is a familiar metaphor for agreeing with it; the counterfactual means that reality itself matched what they desired.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r6.claim: Existential truths are fixed in reality, including God’s oneness, His having no child, and resurrection for recompense; their truth is their actual existence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r6.anchor: مثل كون الإلاه واحدا ، وكونه لا يلد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r7.claim: Moral truths are settled in human conventions and the world’s order: burying girls is injustice, killing is aggression, and gambling takes wealth without right; reversing them would corrupt the world.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r7.anchor: مثل كون الوأد ظلما ، وكون القتل عدوانا ، وكون القمار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r8.claim: Those ‘in them’ means the people inhabiting the heavens and the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p91#2/r8.anchor: أي من في السماوات والأرض من الناس

BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r1.claim: Some say one who submits from fear of punishment or desire for reward submits unwillingly, while one who knows and loves the reward-giver rather than the reward itself submits freely; this is the form valued by God's people.
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : من طالع الثواب والعقاب فاسلم رغبة ورهبة فهو إنما أسلم كرها

BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r2.claim: A thoughtful person should reflect on the Quran, purify faith, and reach knowledge, certainty, and even direct witnessing; God sent His messenger with truth, and anything beyond truth is error.
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r2.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتدبر القرآن فيخلص الإيمان ويصل إلى العرفان والإيقان

BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r3.claim: The truth they dislike includes the Quran brought by the Prophet; the hypothetical means that if revelation conformed to disbelievers' desires, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted and lose order, since order depends on truth such as Islam, oneness, and justice.
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r3.anchor: الذي كرهوه ومن جملته ما جاء به عليه السلام من القرآن

BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r4.claim: The inhabitants included are angels, humans, and jinn, and the cosmos would lose all order if governed by their desires.
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r4.anchor: من الملائكة والإنس والجن وخرجت عن الصلاح والانتظام

BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r5.claim: Some say that without God's command to oppose the ego, people would follow their passions, stray from servitude, abandon divine commands, and be led by desire into Hell.
BURSEVI:v6p67#3/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : لولا أن الله أمر بمخالفة النفوس ومباينتها لاتبع الخلق أهواءهم

BURSEVI:v6p68/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68/r1.claim: The reproach shifts from their dislike of truth to turning from the Qur’an, their worldly and otherworldly honor, which they ought to welcome fully.
BURSEVI:v6p68/r1.anchor: انتقال من تشنيعهم بكراهة الحق الذي يقوم به العالم إلى تشنيعهم بالأعراض عما جبل عليه كل نفس

BURSEVI:v6p68/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p68/r2.claim: “Their reminder” is the Qur’an, their honor and renown in both worlds; 43:44 likewise calls it a reminder for Muhammad and his people.
BURSEVI:v6p68/r2.anchor: والمراد بالذكر القرآن الذي فيه فخرهم وشرفهم في الدنيا والآخرة

BURSEVI:v6p68/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p68/r3.claim: The Qur’an brings what reforms them now and remembrance in the hereafter, but by bad choice they turn from present well-being and their noble end.
BURSEVI:v6p68/r3.anchor: التأويلات النجمية" : {بل أتيناهم} بما فيه لهم صلاح في الحال

BURSEVI:v6p68/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p68/r4.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v6p68/r4.claim: Al-Irshad specifies that they turn away from their own particular pride and honor, rather than from things that merit no attention.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r4.speaker: ابن جريج وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Abū Ṣāliḥ identify “the truth” as God; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this as not fitting the verse's pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج وأبو صالح الحق الله تعالى ع وهذا ليس من نمط الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r5.speaker: غيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r5.claim: Other interpreters take “the truth” as what is right and sound; Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers this because it naturally refers to what Muhammad brought.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r5.anchor: وقال غيرهما الحق هنا الصواب والمستقيم ع وهذا هو الأجرى على أن يكون المذكور قبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r6.claim: If right order followed their desires, the cosmos would be corrupted: they ascribe partners and children to God, negating His exalted attributes, creation, and power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r6.anchor: وذلك أنهم جعلوا لله شركاء وأولادا ولو كان هذا حقا لم تكن لله الصفات العالية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r7.claim: If “the truth” meant God, “following” would mean approving their desires, yet God has allowed unbelieving peoples to persist without cosmic corruption; the wording and consequence become difficult.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r7.anchor: فليس في ذلك فساد سماوات، وأما الحق نفسه الذي هو الصواب فلو كان طبق أهوائهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “their reminder” as God's admonition and clarification to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r8.anchor: بذكرهم يحتمل أن يريد بوعظهم والبيان لهم قاله ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r9.claim: Alternatively, “their reminder” may mean their honor or distinction; this interpretation is also reported.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد بشرفهم، وهو مروي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r10.speaker: ابن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r10.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads the wāw in “law ittabaʿa” with ḍamma; Abū al-Fatḥ calls this rare and likens it to the plural wāw in “ishtaraw.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب «ولو اتبع» بضم الواو وقال أبو الفتح: الضم في هذه الواو قليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r11.claim: Qatāda reads “nudhakkiruhum,” with first-person plural, vocalized and geminated as described in the source.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r11.anchor: وقرأ قتادة «نذكرهم» بنون مضمومة وذال مفتوحة وكسر الكاف مشددة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r12.speaker: عيسى بن عمر وابن أبي إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r12.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read “bal ataytuhum” with first-person singular; Ibn Abī Isḥāq also reads it as a direct address to Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r12.anchor: ابن أبي إسحاق أيضا «بل أتيتهم» خطابا لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r13.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r13.claim: The majority read “bal ataynāhum,” “We brought them.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r14.claim: A report from Abū ʿAmr has the long alif, “ātaynāhum,” meaning “We gave them.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p150#3/r14.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو و «آتيناهم» بالمد بمعنى أعطيناهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r1.claim: One interpretation identifies the Truth with God: if God had made Himself a partner as they wished, all creation would have fallen into disorder.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه الله عز وجل قاله مجاهد وابن جريج والسدي في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r2.claim: Another interpretation identifies the Truth with the Quran: had it endorsed their wish to associate a partner with God, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه القرآن ذكره الفراء والزجاج فعلى القول الأول يكون المعنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r3.claim: Their reminder is the Quran, which gives them honor and distinction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r3.anchor: بل أتيناهم بذكرهم أي بما فيه شرفهم وفخرهم وهو القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r4.claim: They have turned away from the reminder that would bring them distinction in this life and the next.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r4.anchor: فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون أي قد تولوا عما جاءهم من شرف الدنيا والآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وأبو رجاء وأبو الجوزاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r5.claim: These readers say bi-dhikrāhum, with an alif, in both occurrences instead of bi-dhikrihum.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p484#5/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وابو رجاء وابو الجوزاء بل أتيناهم بذكراهم فهم عن ذكراهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد، وأبو صالح والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.claim: They identify al-ḥaqq as God: if God legislated to satisfy people's desires, conflicting desires would corrupt the heavens, earth, and all within them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد، وأبو صالح والسدي: الحق هو الله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r2.claim: Examples of human disagreement show people's incapacity and conflicting opinions, while God is perfect in attributes, speech, acts, law, decree, and governance; no other god or lord exists.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r2.anchor: ففي هذا كله تبيين عجز العباد واختلاف آرائهم وأهوائهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p484#2/r3.claim: The reminder brought to them is the Qur'an, yet they turn away from it.

JISHUMI:v7p5076/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r1.claim: A rational person should follow evidence rather than desire.
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r1.anchor: تدل الآيات على أنه ينبغي للعاقل أن يتبع الأدلة دون الهوى

JISHUMI:v7p5076/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r2.claim: If anything other than God could be worshipped as a deity, religious and worldly order would fail; the verse establishes divine oneness.
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن غير الله لو جاز أن يعبد ويتخد إلها لما استقام الدين والأمر

JISHUMI:v7p5076/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r3.claim: The verse models argument from consequences, showing that a hypothesis would entail corruption.
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r3.anchor: وتدل على طريقة في الحجاج عظيمة؛ لأن المتكلمين أبدا يقولون: لو كان كذا وكذا لأدى إلى فساد

JISHUMI:v7p5076/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r4.claim: The Qurʾan is a remembrance that people should reflect on.
JISHUMI:v7p5076/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن القرآن ذكر يجب التدبر فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r1.claim: The heavens, earth, and their inhabitants stand by truth; if truth followed their desires and became falsehood, the world would lose its foundation and order.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r1.anchor: دل بهذا على عظم شأن الحق ، وأن السماوات والأرض ما قامت ولا من فيهن إلا به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r2.claim: Alternatively, the truth is Islam brought by Muḥammad; if it turned into their shirk, God would bring the Resurrection and destroy the world without delay.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r2.anchor: أو أراد أن الحق الذي جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الإسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r3.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r3.anchor: وعن قتادة : أن الحق هو الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r4.claim: If God followed their desires and commanded shirk and sins, He would be a Satan rather than God and could not uphold the heavens and earth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r4.anchor: ومعناه : لو كان الله إلاها يتبع أهواءهم ويأمر بالشرك والمعاصي ، لما كان إلاها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r5.claim: Bi-dhikrhim can mean the Book that is their reminder, admonition, legacy, or source of pride.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r5.anchor: { بذكرهم } أي بالكتاب الذي هو ذكرهم ، أي : وعظهم أو وصيتهم وفخرهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r6.claim: Alternatively, it is the reminder they had wished for, saying that if they possessed one from earlier peoples they would be sincere servants of God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r6.anchor: أو بالذكر الذي كانوا يتمنونه ويقولون : لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p198/r7.anchor: لكنا عباد الله المخلصين . وقرىء : ( بذكراهم )

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r1.claim: Most commentators identify al-haqq here as God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r1.anchor: في الحق هنا قولان : أحدهما : أنه الله , قاله الأكثرون .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r2.claim: A second view identifies al-haqq as revelation: if it came down according to their wishes, the heavens and earth would be corrupted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه التنزيل أي لو نزل بما يريدون لفسدت السموات والأرض .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r3.claim: The phrase may mean following their desires about what they wish for.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r3.anchor: أحدهما : لو اتبع أهواءهم فيما يشتهونه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r4.claim: Alternatively, it may mean following their desires about what they worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r4.anchor: أحدهما : لو اتبع أهواءهم فيما يشتهونه . الثاني : فيما يعبدونه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r5.claim: One possibility is corruption of the heavens' and earth's governance, since they are governed by truth rather than whim.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r5.anchor: أحدهما : لفسد تدبير السموات والأرض , لأنها مدبرة بالحق لا بالهوى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r6.claim: Another possibility is corruption of their conditions, since they proceed according to wisdom rather than whim.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r6.anchor: الثاني : لفسدت أحوال السموات والأرض لأنها جارية بالحكمة لا على الهوى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r7.claim: “Those within them” means rational beings, namely the angels in heaven and humans on earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r7.anchor: أي ولفسد من فيهن , وذلك إشارة إلى من يعقل من ملائكة السموات وإنس الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r8.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi says it means what is between them; Ibn Masʿud's reading adds “and what is between them,” including irrational animals and inanimate things.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي : يعني ما بينهم من خلق , وفي قراءة ابن مسعود لفسدت السموات والأرض وما بينهما

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads “and the heavens and earth and what is between them”; the standard reading includes rational and irrational beings, since the irrational follow the rational in welfare and corruption.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r9.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود لفسدت السموات والأرض وما بينهما , فتكون على تأويل الكلبي , وقراءة ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r10.claim: Corruption of the angels would mean making them lords though they are subject, and worshipped though they are servants.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r10.anchor: من الفساد ما يعود على من في السموات من الملائكة بأن جعلت أربابا وهي مربوبة , وعبدت وهي مستعبدة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r11.claim: Human corruption takes the form either of destructive submission to desire or unbelief through worshipping other than God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r11.anchor: وفساد الإنس يكون على وجهين : أحدهما : باتباع الهوى . وذلك مهلك . الثاني : بعبادة غير الله . وذلك كفر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r12.claim: The jinn's corruption would come from being obeyed and becoming tyrannical; other things are corrupted dependently because rational beings manage them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r12.anchor: وأما فساد الجن فيكون بأن يطاعوا فيطغوا . وأما فساد ما عدا ذلك فيكون على وجه التبع بأنهم مدبرون بذوي العقول .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says “their reminder” means clarification of truth for them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r13.anchor: أحدهما : عنى ببيان الحق لهم , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r14.speaker: السدي وسفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r14.claim: Al-Suddi and Sufyan say it means their honor, since the Messenger is one of them and the Qurʾan is in their language.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r15.claim: A third possibility is a reminder of the duties incumbent on them and the reward they are owed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r15.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : بذكر ما عليهم من طاعة ولهم من جزاء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r16.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r16.claim: Qatada says that turning away from their reminder means turning away from the Qurʾan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r16.anchor: أحدهما : فهم عن القرآن معرضون , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r17.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r17.claim: Al-Suddi says they turn away from their own honor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p61/r17.anchor: الثاني : عن شرفهم معرضون , قاله السدي .

MUQATIL:23:66-71/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r13.claim: If God followed Meccan unbelievers' desires, He would associate a partner with Himself and the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would perish.
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r13.anchor: يقول الله، عز وجل: { ولو اتبع الحق أهوآءهم } يعني لو اتبع الله أهواء كفار مكة،

MUQATIL:23:66-71/r14.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r14.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r14.claim: Their reminder and honor is the Qur'an.
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r14.anchor: بل أتيناهم بذكرهم } يعني بشرفهم يعني القرآن { فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون

MUQATIL:23:66-71/r15.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r15.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r15.claim: They turn away from the Qur'an and do not believe in it.
MUQATIL:23:66-71/r15.anchor: فهم عن ذكرهم معرضون } [آية: 71] يعني القرآن معرضون عنه فلا يؤمنون به.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r2.claim: If God followed their desires concerning the gods they believe in, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r2.anchor: ﴿ أهواءهم ﴾ فيما يعتقدون من الآلهة ﴿ لفسدت السماوات ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r3.claim: He supports this argument with the verse saying that if there were gods besides God in heaven and earth, both would be corrupted.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r3.anchor: كما قال لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r4.claim: Rational beings are singled out because everything else follows them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r4.anchor: خص العقلاء بالذكر لأن غيرهم تبع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r5.claim: Their reminder is the Book, which admonishes them and honors them because the Messenger is one of them and the Quran is in their language.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r5.anchor: بالكتاب الذى هو ذكرهم أى وعظهم أو شرفهم لأن الرسول منهم والقرآن بلغتهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r6.claim: Alternatively, it means the reminder they had wished for, saying, “If only we had a reminder from earlier peoples.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r6.anchor: أو بالذكر الذى كانوا يتمنونه ويقولون لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين الآية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p126#8/r7.claim: Their turning away from the reminder is by their own bad choice.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r1.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج وأبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r1.claim: Most commentators, including Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj, and Abu Salih, identify “the truth” here as God, exalted is He.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r1.anchor: هنا هو الله سبحانه وتعالى قاله الأكثرون، منهم مجاهد وابن جريج وأبو صالح

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r2.claim: Al-Nahhas supplies the implied Arabic sense: “if the possessor of truth followed” their desires.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r2.anchor: وتقديره في العربية: ولو اتبع صاحب الحق قاله النحاس

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r3.claim: One gloss takes “following” metaphorically as truth agreeing with their desires: if they could disbelieve and disobey without punishment through divine incapacity or ignorance, the heavens and earth would be corrupted.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r3.anchor: وقد قيل: هو مجاز، أي لو وافق الحق أهواءهم فجعل موافقته اتباعا مجازا

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r4.claim: Another view says that if the truth were their claim that God has partners, the gods would disagree in their aims, disrupting governance and corrupting the heavens and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r4.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ولو كان الحق ما يقولون من اتخاذ آلهة مع الله تعالى لتنافت الآلهة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r5.claim: Another reading says the world’s order would fail if truth followed human cravings, since desires differ and conflict; truth is to be followed and people must submit to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r5.anchor: وقيل: «لو اتبع الحق أهواءهم» أي بما يهواه الناس ويشتهونه لبطل نظام العالم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r6.claim: A further view takes “the truth” as the Qur’an: if it had been revealed according to what they liked, the heavens and earth would be corrupted.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r6.anchor: وقيل: «الحق» القرآن أي لو نزل القرآن بما يحبون لفسدت السموات والأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r7.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r7.claim: Al-Mawardi says “whoever is in them” refers to rational beings: the angels in the heavens and humans and jinn on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى من يعقل من ملائكة السموات وإنس الأرض وجنها الماوردي

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r8.claim: Ibn Masud’s recitation reads “and what is between them”; al-Kalbi likewise understands the phrase to include creatures between heaven and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعني وما بينهما من خلق وهي قراءة ابن مسعود «لفسدت السموات والأرض وما بينهما»

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r9.claim: On al-Kalbi’s explanation and Ibn Masud’s reading, corruption includes rational and nonrational beings, animals, and inanimate things.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r9.anchor: فيكون على تأويل الكلبي وقراءة ابن مسعود محمولا على فساد من يعقل وما لا يعقل من حيوان وجماد

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r10.claim: The majority reading’s apparent sense concerns rational creatures, since what lacks reason follows rational beings in their soundness or corruption.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r10.anchor: وظاهر التنزيل في قراءة الجمهور يكون محمولا على فساد ما يعقل من الحيوان لأن ما لا يعقل تابع لما يعقل

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r11.claim: Angel corruption would mean treating as lords those who are themselves governed, and worshipping beings who are themselves servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r11.anchor: فعلى هذا ما يكون من الفساد يعود على من في السموات من الملائكة بأن جعلت أربابا وهي مربوبة، وعبدت وهي مستعبدة

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r12.claim: Human corruption takes two forms: following desire, which is ruinous, and worshipping other than God, which is unbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r12.anchor: وفساد الإنس يكون على وجهين: أحدهما: باتباع الهوى، وذلك مهلك. الثاني: بعبادة غير الله، وذلك كفر

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r13.claim: Corruption of the rest of creation is consequential, because it is governed by rational beings and their corruption reaches what they manage.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r13.anchor: وأما فساد ما عدا ذلك فيكون على وجه التبع لأنهم مدبرون بذوي العقول فعاد فساد المدبرين عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r14.speaker: السدي وسفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r14.claim: Al-Suddi and Sufyan explain “their reminder” as what brings them honor and prestige.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r14.anchor: أي بما فيه شرفهم وعزهم قاله السدي وسفيان

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r15.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r15.claim: Qatada explains it as what contains mention of their reward and punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r15.anchor: وقال قتادة: أي بما لهم فيه ذكر ثوابهم وعقابهم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas understands it as clarification of the truth and of the religious matters they need.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r16.anchor: ابن عباس: أي ببيان الحق وذكر ما لهم به حاجة من أمر الدين

QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:71/r17.claim: Despite receiving this reminder, they turn away from it.

QASHANI:23:71/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:71/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:71/r1.claim: Truth means unity and justice, the call to Essence and attributes; following the desires of plural, veiled souls would destroy justice sustaining heaven and earth and unity sustaining immaterial realities.
QASHANI:23:71/r1.anchor: الذي هو التوحيد والعدل، أي الدعوة إلى الذات والصفات { أهواءهم } المتفرقة في الباطل

QASHANI:23:71/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:71/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:71/r2.claim: Unity preserves the realities of things, while its shadow, justice and the ordering of multiplicity, sustains heaven and earth; losing both would corrupt all.
QASHANI:23:71/r2.anchor: إذ بالوحدة بقاء حقائق الأشياء، وبظلها الذي هو العدل ونظام الكثرات قوام الأرض والسماء

QASHANI:23:71/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:23:71/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:23:71/r3.claim: The straight path is unity, bringing justice to the soul, love to the heart, and witnessing of unity to the spirit; those veiled by sensation, impurity, and multiplicity are steeped in injustice and hostility and veer away from it.
QASHANI:23:71/r3.anchor: طريق التوحيد المستلزم لحصول العدالة في النفس ووجود المحبة في القلب وشهود الوحدة في الروح

RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r16.claim: The duty is to abandon desire and follow truth; if truth followed human desires, grave corruption would result.
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r16.anchor: الواجب على المكلف أن يطرح الهوى ويتبع الحق

RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r17.claim: One explanation is that the polytheists thought associating gods with God was true; that would corrupt the cosmos, as in the argument against multiple gods.
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r17.anchor: القوم كانوا يرون أن الحق في اتخاذ آلهة مع الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r18.claim: Another explanation is that their desires were idol worship and denial of Muḥammad, sources of corruption; truth is Islam, and following them would require ending the world.
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r18.anchor: أن أهواءهم في عبادة الأوثان وتكذيب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r19.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r19.claim: Al-Qaffāl says their opinions contradicted one another, so following them would cause contradiction and collapse the world’s order.
RAZI-FULL:v23p96#2/r19.anchor: آراءهم كانت متناقضة فلو اتبع الحق أهواءهم لوقع التناقض ولاختل نظام العالم عن القفال

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r1.claim: “Their reminder” can mean Qurʾān and proofs, or their honor and glory through the Messenger; these readings are close because Messenger and proofs establish one another.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r1.anchor: قيل إنه القرآن والأدلة وقيل بل شرفهم وفخرهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r2.claim: Another interpretation is admonition and warning.

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r3.claim: It may mean the scripture they wished for, recalling their claim that they would be devoted servants if given a reminder from earlier peoples.
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r3.anchor: وقيل هو الذي كانوا يتمنونه ويقولون

RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r4.claim: A variant reading is bidhikrāhum, “their reminder.”
RAZI-FULL:v23p98/r4.anchor: لكنا عباد الله المخلصين } ( الصافات : 168 ، 169 ) وقرىء بذكراهم

STUDYQURAN:23:71/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r1.claim: One interpretation is, “If the truth were in accord with their desires.”
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r1.anchor: is understood to mean, “If the truth were in accord with their desires” (Q)

STUDYQURAN:23:71/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r2.claim: Another interpretation is, “If the upholder of truth were to obey their desires.”
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r2.anchor: or “If the upholder of truth were to obey their desires” (Q)

STUDYQURAN:23:71/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r3.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r3.claim: A metaphysical reading says that if reality matched their desires, the heavens and earth would fall into disorder because human desires are chaotic and conflict with each other.
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r3.anchor: It may also be interpreted metaphysically to mean that if reality were to be as they desired, the order of the heavens and earth would be corrupted

STUDYQURAN:23:71/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r4.claim: The reminder refers to the Quran and the truths it contains.
STUDYQURAN:23:71/r4.anchor: The reminder refers to the Quran and the truths it contains (R)

TAB-FULL:v17p89/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r1.claim: If God governed by the polytheists' desires and left the truth they dislike, creation would be ruined: they do not know consequences or sound governance, and most favor falsehood over truth; the heavens and earth stand by truth.
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم} [المؤمنون: 71] قال: " الحق: الله "

TAB-FULL:v17p89/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r2.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ, in reports transmitted by al-Suddī and Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, identifies al-ḥaqq here as God.
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح: {ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم} [المؤمنون: 71] قال: «الله»

TAB-FULL:v17p89/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj likewise says al-ḥaqq means God.
TAB-FULL:v17p89/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم} [المؤمنون: 71] قال: " الحق: الله "

TAB-FULL:v17p90/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “We brought them their reminder” as “We made [it] clear to them.”
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {بل أتيناهم بذكرهم} [المؤمنون: 71] يقول: بينا لهم

TAB-FULL:v17p90/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r2.claim: Other interpreters say dhikr means their honor, since the Qur'an descended upon a man from their own people; they compare 43:44.
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: بل أتيناهم بشرفهم؛ وذلك أن هذا القرآن كان شرفا لهم، لأنه نزل على رجل منهم

TAB-FULL:v17p90/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the interpretations are close: the Qur'an explains what people need for their religion and is also a remembrance and honor for the Messenger and his people.
TAB-FULL:v17p90/r3.anchor: وهذان القولان متقاربا المعنى. وذلك أن الله جل ثناؤه أنزل هذا القرآن بيانا بين فيه ما لخلقه إليه الحاجة

SULAMI:v2p37#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p37#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p37#2/r1.claim: Without God’s command to oppose the self, people would follow its desires, stray from servitude, abandon God’s commands and obedience, and persist in opposition.
SULAMI:v2p37#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : لولا أن الله أمر بمخالفة النفوس ومباينتها لاتبع الخلق أهواءهم

SULAMI:v2p37#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p37#2/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p37#2/r2.claim: God first disclosed the realities to creatures, then the means, tranquility, and insight; when they witnessed the Real through the Real, they renounced every aspiration and will.
SULAMI:v2p37#2/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله في هذه الآية : أول ما كاشف الله خلقه كاشفهم بالمعارف

TABATABAI:23:70-71/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:70-71/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:70-71/r4.claim: They want the true call to follow their desires, but if caprice governed belief and conduct, idolatry, denial of revelation and resurrection, and corruption would follow; desire has no stable limit, so the cosmic order would collapse.
TABATABAI:23:70-71/r4.anchor: إذ لو اتبع الحق أهواءهم فتركوا وما يهوونه من الاعتقاد والعمل فعبدوا الأصنام واتخذوا الأرباب ونفوا الرسالة والمعاد

TABATABAI:23:70-71/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:70-71/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:70-71/r5.claim: More precisely, humanity is existentially bound to the cosmos, has a species goal of happiness and an ordained path, and is equipped by cosmic and human nature for the beliefs and actions leading there; religion follows this order and fitrah.
TABATABAI:23:70-71/r5.anchor: أن الإنسان حقيقة كونية مرتبطة في وجودها بالكون العام وله في نوعيته غاية هي سعادته وقد خط له طريق إلى سعادته

TABATABAI:23:71/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:71/r1.claim: Human life’s route to happiness is fixed by the true order disclosed in human nature and the cosmic system, which God decreed; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī links this to 30:30.
TABATABAI:23:71/r1.anchor: فسنة الحياة التي تنتهي بسالكها إلى السعادة الإنسانية طريقة متعينة يقتضيها النظام بالحق

TABATABAI:23:71/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:71/r2.claim: If the truth conformed to their whims, cosmic elements, causes, and regular relations would have to change into arbitrary, conflicting relations, corrupting the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants.
TABATABAI:23:71/r2.anchor: فلو اتبع الحق أهواءهم فاقتضى لهم من الشرع ما تجازف به أهواؤهم لم يكن ذلك إلا بتغير أجزاء الكون عما هي عليه

TABATABAI:23:71/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:71/r3.claim: Cosmic existence and its governance are inseparable, as are creation and command; this is why changing the order would corrupt both the world and its administration.
TABATABAI:23:71/r3.anchor: لأن كينونتها وتدبيرها مختلطان غير متمايزين، والخلق والأمر متصلان غير منفصلين

TABATABAI:23:71/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:71/r4.claim: The ‘reminder’ is the Qur’an, as in 21:50 and 43:44.
TABATABAI:23:71/r4.anchor: لا ريب أن المراد بالذكر هو القرآن كما قال

TABATABAI:23:71/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:71/r5.claim: Calling it a reminder after the charge that the Prophet was possessed counterposes their insult that the bearer of the reminder was mad (15:6).
TABATABAI:23:71/r5.anchor: ولعل التعبير عنه بالذكر بعد قوله

TABATABAI:23:71/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:71/r6.claim: The Qur’an reminds them of God or recalls God’s religion of true belief and good works; the latter sense better fits the preceding context.
TABATABAI:23:71/r6.anchor: لأنه يذكرهم بالله أو يذكر لهم دين الله

TABATABAI:23:71/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:71/r7.claim: The reminder is called ‘their’ religion because the true call varies in generality and detail among peoples, and this final revelation is the last stage of detailed law; they reject the religion proper to them.
TABATABAI:23:71/r7.anchor: وإنما أضيف إليهم لأن الدين أعني الدعوة الحقة مختلفة بالنسبة إلى الناس بالإجمال والتفصيل والذي يذكره القرآن آخر مراحل التفصيل

TABATABAI:23:71/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:71/r8.speaker: كثير منهم
TABATABAI:23:71/r8.claim: Many commentators take the possessive ‘their reminder’ as an honorific; they compare the phrase to the Qur’an’s statement that it is a reminder for the Prophet and his people (43:44).
TABATABAI:23:71/r8.anchor: وقال كثير منهم إن إضافة الذكر إليهم للتشريف نظير قوله

TABATABAI:23:72/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:72/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:72/r1.claim: Although the Qur’an honors the Prophet, his household, Arabs, and the community, ‘their’ denotes this religion’s specific relation to the community, which fits the context better.
TABATABAI:23:72/r1.anchor: غير أن الإضافة في الآية ليست لهذه العناية بل لعناية اختصاص هذا الدين بهذه الأمة وهو الأوفق لصدر الآية

TABRISI:23:71/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:71/r1.speaker: أبو صالح، ابن جريج، السدي
TABRISI:23:71/r1.claim: Abu Salih, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Suddi identify al-haqq as God: making Him a partner as disbelievers wish would corrupt the heavens and earth.
TABRISI:23:71/r1.anchor: الحق هو الله تعالى عن أبي صالح وابن جريج والسدي والمعنى ولو جعل الله لنفسه شريكا

TABRISI:23:71/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:71/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:23:71/r2.claim: Another view takes truth as what calls to benefits and desires as what call to harms; following desires would corrupt the cosmos.
TABRISI:23:71/r2.anchor: وقيل: الحق ما يدعو إلى المصالح والمحاسن والأهواء ما تدعو إلى المفاسد والمقابح

TABRISI:23:71/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:71/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:23:71/r3.claim: Another view says affairs would be corrupted because the cosmos follows wisdom, not whims; “those in them” means rational beings among angels, humans, and jinn.
TABRISI:23:71/r3.anchor: وقيل: معناه لفسدت أحوال السماوات والأرض لأنها جارية على الحكمة لا على الهوى

TABRISI:23:71/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:71/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:23:71/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says “those in them” includes all creatures between heaven and earth.
TABRISI:23:71/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: وما بينهما من خلق فيكون عاما

TABRISI:23:71/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:71/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:71/r5.claim: Following desire invalidates proofs and confidence in them, destroys trust in promises and threats, and could reverse a wise ruler’s justice.
TABRISI:23:71/r5.anchor: ووجه فساد العالم بذلك أنه يوجب بطلان الأدلة وامتناع الثقة بالمدلول عليه

TABRISI:23:71/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:71/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:71/r6.claim: God gave them honor through a messenger from among them and the Quran in their language, but they turn away and accept humiliation.
TABRISI:23:71/r6.anchor: أي بما فيه شرفهم وفخرهم لأن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم والقرآن بلسانهم

TABRISI:23:71/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:71/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:23:71/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets dhikr as clarification of the truth.
TABRISI:23:71/r7.anchor: وقيل: الذكر البيان للحق عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v7p52/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p52/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p52/r3.claim: Here al-haqq means God: if He acted according to their desires, the heavens, earth, and all within them would become corrupt.
THALABI:v7p52/r3.anchor: ولو اتبع الحق يعني الله سبحانه أهواءهم مرادهم فيما يفعل لفسدت السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن

THALABI:v7p52/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p52/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p52/r4.claim: Their reminder, clarification, and honor is the Qur’an, yet they turn away from it.
THALABI:v7p52/r4.anchor: بل أتيناهم بذكرهم ببيانهم وشرفهم يعني القرآن.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p299#2/r1.claim: Dhikruhum here means their honor or renown.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r1.speaker: أبو صالح، ابن جريج، مقاتل، السدي، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r1.claim: These authorities take الحق as God; if He had taken the partner they wished for, the heavens and earth would have been corrupted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو صالح (¬6)، وابن جريج (¬7)، ومقاتل (¬8)، والسدي (¬9)، والكلبي (¬10): الحق هو الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r2.speaker: الفراء، الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj allow الحق to mean revelation sent according to their wishes, such as affirming partners and deities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء والزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بالحق -هاهنا-: التنزيل، أي: نزل بما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r3.claim: The verse echoes the proof that if there were gods besides God in the heavens and earth, both would be corrupted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r3.anchor: كقوله تعالى: {لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا} [الأنبياء: 22]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r4.claim: Truth calls to virtues and whims to vices; following their whims would make truth call to corruption, invalidate proofs and confidence in conclusions, and multiply disorder.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p34#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: الحق لما كان يدعو إلى المحاسن والأهواء تدعو إلى المقابح؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r1.claim: The Qur'an brought them what would confer their honor and renown.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares this to the Book sent to the people and the Qur'an as a remembrance for Muhammad and his people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو كقوله: {لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا} [الأنبياء: 10]: وقوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r3.claim: They turned away from what had come to them and could bring honor in this life and the next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p35/r3.anchor: يريد تولوا عما جاء به من شرف الدنيا والآخرة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r1.claim: The Truth is the Qur'an, which calls to good, while their desires call to evil; if revelation matched their wishes, it would call to polytheism and the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r1.anchor: القرآن الذي يدعو إلى المحاسن { أهواءهم } التي تدعو إلى المقابح

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r2.claim: The heavens and earth are signs of God's oneness; a Qur'an tailored to their wishes would promote polytheism and undermine those proofs, as its followers would associate partners with God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r2.anchor: وذلك أنها خلقت دلالة على توحيد الله، فلو كان القرآن على مرادهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:71-72/r3.claim: The reminder brought to them is their honor in this world and the next.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p409#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p409#2/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p409#2/r9.claim: The desires in question are those of the polytheists.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r1.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r1.claim: Hasan says that if truth followed their desires, those desires would bring ruin on the heavens, earth, and everyone in them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r1.anchor: وتفسير الحسن: لو كان الحق في أهوائهم، لوقعت أهواؤهم على هلاك السموات والأرض ومن فيهن

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r2.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r2.claim: Some interpret al-haqq here as God, citing the command to counsel one another with truth as meaning God and with patience as steadfastness in His duties.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الحق هاهنا: الله، كقوله: {وتواصوا بالحق} [العصر: 3] يعني بالحق: الله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p410/r3.speaker: author
